- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts longer than observed price behavior suggests.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history includes strong upward momentum.
- Model underreacts to sharp downward moves in recent history — fails to anticipate sudden drops or corrections.
- When true outcome is significantly lower than forecast, model often fails to adjust downward in the next forecast window — suggesting poor lag correction.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — if price was high recently, it keeps forecasting high even when data suggests a correction is imminent.
- Overshooting after spikes is common — model may peak too early or too high, then fail to adjust as price stabilizes or declines.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — often misses sharp corrections or sudden reversals.
- When true outcome is lower than forecast, model often doesn’t reduce forecast by enough — suggesting poor downward bias correction.
